stories.name: Hoàn Kiếm Lake
stories.title: The lake where the sword was returned
stories.summary: Legend has it that Emperor Lê Lợi returned a magical sword to the Golden Turtle God in this lake in the 15th century, which is where its name comes from: the Lake of the Returned Sword. The Turtle Tower on its small island is the city's emblem.

stories.name: One Pillar Pagoda
stories.title: A pagoda on a single stone pillar
stories.summary: Emperor Lý Thái Tông built the pagoda in 1049, and it stands on one stone pillar in the middle of a lotus pond - a shape meant to recall a lotus flower rising from the water. The French destroyed the original in 1954; what stands today is a reconstruction.

stories.name: Thánh địa Mỹ Sơn
stories.title: The Champa temples in the valley
stories.summary: The Champa kingdom built Hindu temples here between the 4th and 14th centuries, in a valley ringed by hills. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and parts of it were damaged by bombing in the 20th century.

stories.name: Phố cổ Hội An
stories.title: A port where merchants met
stories.summary: Hội An was a trading port from the 15th to the 19th century, where Japanese, Chinese and European merchants met. Its Japanese Covered Bridge dates from the 1590s, and the town survived the wars that flattened much of central Vietnam.

stories.name: Thành nhà Hồ
stories.title: A citadel of stone blocks
stories.summary: The Hồ dynasty built this citadel in 1397, with walls of large stone blocks fitted without mortar. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 2011.

stories.name: Cố đô Huế
stories.title: The Nguyễn capital
stories.summary: Huế was the capital of the Nguyễn dynasty from 1802 to 1945. Inside the Citadel lies the Imperial Enclosure, with the Forbidden Purple City at its centre; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

stories.name: Vịnh Hạ Long
stories.title: Sixteen hundred islands of limestone
stories.summary: Ha Long Bay holds around 1,600 limestone islands and islets, most of them too steep to live on. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.

stories.name: Địa đạo Củ Chi
stories.title: A city underground
stories.summary: During the Vietnam War the Viet Cong dug a network of tunnels at Củ Chi with living areas, kitchens and hospitals below ground, and several levels stacked under each other. Parts of it are open to visitors today.
